title: President Richard III Announces Sweeping Reforms in Coronation Address
subtitle: A bold policy agenda from one of Shakespeare's most loathsome villains
body_html:
Lords and ladies, we are gathered here today to celebrate me. It's very, very cold out, some have called us the winter of our discontent. Those were our leading weathermen. I am gonna turn this kingdom around, and we're gonna make this glorious summer. They will not be any more clouds. Today, I will sign a royal decree for the purpose of relocating all the clouds into the bottom of the ocean. Yes, that's correct, under my administration, there will be no more clouds, because we will round them up, and buried will they be. It'll be sunshine every day, no more clouds, you'll see.

We're also gonna get rid of war. Have you seen the grim visage of war? We're gonna smooth its wrinkled front. We're gonna use Botox. Because we have that now, thanks to scientists. Instead of getting on frightful seeds— that's horses that are scary— there's gonna be capering nimbly. I'm very good at capering, and I'm very nimble. There will be no more war, and because of it, we're gonna get to spend more time with ladies. We're gonna go into their rooms, and it's gonna be great. No one will complain, there will only be ladies and men, and nothing else, and we're gonna go into their rooms, or, as we used to call them, chambers.

We are going to make rooms chambers again!

[awkward pause for applause, which, not occuing, leads to the resumption of the address]

What kind of high jinx will we get into? First, there is going to be sexy music. We're gonna bring back lute education, and we're going to teach all the musicians how to play lute. Originally, I said I was gonna get rid of the National Endowment for the Arts, but now we're funding it, even bigger, we're gonna have the biggest arts that have ever been, and it's all gonna be lascivious music, and it's all gonna be for capering in ladies’ chambers, and it's all gonna be on the lute, cause that's the best instrument.

I have extended a pardon to Richard “R.” Kelly. He will become our new appointee for the head of the National Endowment for the Arts. No one knows how to make sexy music better than R. Kelly, and he has served his time. His sentence is here by pardoned. He’s been trapped in the closet too long, a hostage of the closet, and by royal decree, a prisoner no more. He will, God willing, be bumping and grinding in ‘da Club tonight. Know this, friends, that it is time, again, for Ignition. I believe he can fly, also, and thus is is so.

Some of us have not been made as attractive as others, and many men, who I have heard are called uncles? Oh, I'm sorry, incels, they feel they are entitled to wonton nymphs. They feel they have been curtailed of their fair proportion of tail. And they shall have it, thanks to me. I'm passing an executive order that applies to all Stacys, each of which will be allocated to an incel.

There have been rumors that Chads are immigrants, they're not from here, and those Chads, they are going to be imprisoned. And then we're gonna round them up, round up all the Chads, who’ve been taking up all the Stacys, taking them away from the good hard-working incels, and and we're gonna deal with them.

In our kingdom, even if you're not very attractive, when you look in the mirror, things feel bad. Even if you're so horrible looking that dogs bark at you—because you're so scary looking? You're still gonna have a Stacy, too.

I want say a few words about the former King. He was not a very good king, and I've heard some dreadful prophecies. Apparently, the king was bad. He was very bad, and we're not going to allow it. I've heard libels, dreadful, bad, bad things, and we're not gonna stand for it anymore. You know, back in the day, when someone did a bad thing, we didn't have to wait for a jury, or for a judge. The king could issue a decree, and that person would be putting in the Tower of London. We would refer to that as being closely mewed up. Those were the words we used in history. I’m a fan of history, a leading historian myself. I'm not saying our current King is bad, because that king is me, but previous kings have been very bad. Do you know Kings have a Divine Right?

Additionally, I've decided to create a new religion, divorce Melania, no matter what the pope says. The lady Anne, however is very appealing. I'm gonna marry her instead, and maybe take a mistress, and probably play some R. Kelly on the lute, while I keep her in my chambers.

No more clouds, no more Chads, it's a new day. Only sunshine. Thank you for attending my coronation.1

[end scene one]

Later that day, a list of pardons was announced, and the follwing individuals were allowed out of federal prison:

  • Iago

  • Lady Macbeth

  • Macbeth

  • Claudius

  • Edmund

  • Aaron the Moor

  • Goneril and Regan

  • Don John

  • Malvolio

  • Shylock

  • Parolles

  • Duke Frederick

  • King John

  • Queen Margaret

  • Cardinal Wolsey

  • Jack Cade

For the few of you who haven't memorized the play Richard III, here is the scene this article is a parody of:

Now is the winter of our discontent
Made glorious summer by this son of York,
And all the clouds that loured upon our house
In the deep bosom of the ocean buried.
Now are our brows bound with victorious wreaths,
Our bruisèd arms hung up for monuments,
Our stern alarums changed to merry meetings,
Our dreadful marches to delightful measures.
Grim-visaged war hath smoothed his wrinkled front;
And now, instead of mounting barbèd steeds
To fright the souls of fearful adversaries,
He capers nimbly in a lady’s chamber
To the lascivious pleasing of a lute.
But I, that am not shaped for sportive tricks,
Nor made to court an amorous looking glass;
I, that am rudely stamped and want love’s majesty
To strut before a wanton ambling nymph;
I, that am curtailed of this fair proportion,
Cheated of feature by dissembling nature,
Deformed, unfinished, sent before my time
Into this breathing world scarce half made up,
And that so lamely and unfashionable
That dogs bark at me as I halt by them—

Why, I, in this weak piping time of peace,
Have no delight to pass away the time,
Unless to see my shadow in the sun
And descant on mine own deformity.
And therefore, since I cannot prove a lover
To entertain these fair well-spoken days,
I am determinèd to prove a villain
And hate the idle pleasures of these days.
Plots have I laid, inductions dangerous,
By drunken prophecies, libels, and dreams,
To set my brother Clarence and the King
In deadly hate, the one against the other;
And if King Edward be as true and just
As I am subtle, false, and treacherous,
This day should Clarence closely be mewed up
About a prophecy which says that “G”
Of Edward’s heirs the murderer shall be.
Dive, thoughts, down to my soul. Here Clarence
comes.
